title: `.env` files are ephemeral regenerable reflections of the manifest, never the source of truth
description: A `.env` file, when it exists on a developer laptop or a CI runner, is a per-machine reflection generated on demand from the Secrets Manager by an env reflector command (`secrets reflect`). The reflector reads the current manifest slice for the target process, fetches the values, and writes them to the `.env` path atomically; a subsequent `secrets reflect` overwrites the file. The `.env` path is gitignored at project root; the manifest is committed. A process that reads `.env` directly at boot instead of going through the Secrets Manager client is a v1 policy violation caught by the source-tree scan the CI gate runs. The `.env` reflection is a convenience for local tooling that expects one; it is never the authoritative store, it is never rotated in-place, and it is discardable at any moment.
rationale: `.env` files were invented as a laptop-local shim and have quietly become primary state on many projects, which is where rotation drift, uncommitted-secret-shape drift, and shared-laptop leaks begin. Recentring the manifest as the source of truth and demoting `.env` to a projection removes both classes of drift without breaking the local-dev flow developers already have muscle memory for.
